There are a lot of interesting things about berserk. For one, never have i encountered a bad guy who i hate as much as Griffith.

As such, i can understand why the Author has to take so many hiatuses. a good story like this takes time, and probably is traumatic as well to create.

But where does the inspiration come from?

On one hand(PUN!!!!!), Guts strikes me as Odin, one eyed, dour, hates his son. With Zodd as Balder, indestructible, and most likely to be killed through some crazy nature magic means.

But, Griffith strikes me as Macbeth. He has built an empire, everything is going well, but ultimately, it will fall due to his actions and the curses he has brought upon himself. This is compounded by the witches, and the fact that everyone is going to Avalon.

So what is everyone's thoughts on this? As we wait for some awesome person to translate 338 for us Gaijin.
[Discussion]Is berserk a re-imagining of Norse mythology, or is it more like a reinterpretation of MacBeth?

Berserk is an outsider's interpretation of a culturally alien mythography. Essentially, Berserk is a classic Western fantasy story warped by pop culture and filtered through a mind steeped in Eastern thought. That's why it feels so strange and fresh. It's culturally disjointed, borrowing, not from a singular source, but rather all of Western lore.

It is as wonderful, as it is horrible, which is something that is extremely rare.

It has all the elements: love, betrayal, adversity, friendship; but it does not hold back in the slightest. Its like reading a fairytale from back in the 1600s, in its full gory nature.

I am following it, because i want to see Griffith die. so i am trying to find whatever meaning i can to set me at ease until he dies...

though i have some horrible thoughts, like what if the new behilt is Casca's, not Guts, and SHE will betray him next?

As difficult as it may be, consider that Griffith may have not been wrong. He's a piece of shit, but he's never betrayed his dream. He sacrificed dozens of his close friends, yes, but how many thousands did they kill? How many dreams were slaughtered to satisfy the desires of mad nobles? When weighed against the madness of their world, Griffith's crimes are small and personal. Perhaps, that's why you hate him.

No,

I hate him, because he betrayed his subordinates, to the point of raping one of his lieutenants. That is one of the greatest sins, especially for a military force, to betray your subordinates. That is why i hate him.

What would have happened had he said no? Would he not have been a king?

He had an army, the old king was sick, he and the country was being invaded. He could have gained his empire, through the old fashioned way. He was respected by the other nobles, he could have easily been king.

But did he get his dream? We think he did, but all throughout myth, this is the setup for the greatest fall.

Guts was born from a hung women, in a tree. Now there is a giant tree in that kingdom, and we really do not understand what guts is. We assume he is human. but there are things that are off about him. Where did he go for that year? Why was he able to survive and thrive in war so well? What is the source of this supernatural anger.

A normal man will not cut his arm off to get at someone. That rage, is supernatural, and is similar to some stories about Odin. Then there is the name, Guts. The reason why it shows up a lot in anime and video games, is because it is connected to Buddhism, as the warrior aspect of Buddha.

http://www.beyondthenet.net/thedway/soldier.htm this is an interesting source, because it not just talks about soldiers, but also kings, and a lot of what is seen in berserk, is mentioned here. Griffith would be an impure king.

I traveled trough out Asia when i was in the navy, i saw a lot of Buddhism in the different parts of the world, and read about it. The more i read about it, and the more i read berserk, the more i interpret Guts to be a war aspect of Buddha. but because such aspects are rare, its really hard to tell, and i could just be overthinking things.

Frankly there are not enough issues of the manga to draw a good conclusion. But Guts does embody a lot of the higher warrior aspects mentioned in mention sutras.

We are using GMT as our time/day for when to change the date. For a reference as to what day is what date, here is a table:

IRL Day ModernPowers Date
Monday January/February
Tuesday March/April
Wednesday May/June
Thursday July/August
Friday September/October
Saturday November/December
Sunday Meta-Day

Meaning one IRL week is equal to one ModernPowers year.

Sunday is known as meta-day, where you may only submit [Meta], [News] and [Roleplay]. You CANNOT submit any other type of post than them or it will be deleted/marked invalid. These posts should not affect the gameplay of the sub and should focus on discussion, recent summaries and descriptions of your country. [Claim] posts are always available to new users.

Also, for confusion about which month is when, AM (morning) is the first month, and PM (afternoon) is the second month. For example, on Thursday, before lunch time would be July, and after lunch time would be August.

So if you are confused as to why the dates have been changing so frequently, hopefully this should clear up some things.

It depends on what you are "knowing when you see it"

Is it a questionable image that could be CP, then yeah, trash that. Seem's like it could lead to someone getting doxxed, of course. I don't feel you are gonna have rules that cover all those situations 100%, so "I know it when I see it" is a solid rule in those cases.

But there are abuses to that, like the TTP stuff not being "news" that do rub me the wrong way.

Deleting stuff that is totally not even close to the idea of you sub, sure? But stuff like /r/news and the TTP is what we should be aiming to cut out.

"I'll know it when I see it" is an easy rule to fall back on, but I think it should only come after exhausting every other attempt to pin down specific and detailed rules. Transparency and specific detailed rules are much harder to use in an overly broad manner and much less prone to selective enforcement. Sometimes being a fair and transparent moderator means limiting your own power a little bit, and that can be a frightening thing to do when a subverse is your baby. But I think the effort is worthwhile, and it's something larger communities encounter more often than smaller communities.
I'm just glad modlogs are a thing so we can call out bullshit moderation practices.
